cohort: 960 indoor patients treated under the Chief Minister Arogya Arunachal Yojana/Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (CMAAY/PMJAY) insurance schemes at Tomo Riba Institute of Health and Medical Sciences (TRIHMS) in Arunachal Pradesh, North East India, from June 2020 to December 2020.
finding: The most common antimicrobial agent used was ceftriaxone (54.1%), followed by cefuroxime (17.5%), metronidazole (10%), and cefoperazone (7.5%); the most common antiulcer drug used was pantoprazole (76.25%); and the most commonly used analgesics were diclofenac sodium (53.3%), followed by tramadol (30.6%), pentazocine (23.3%), and paracetamol (20.2%).
